## Proof

We evaluate
$$I = \int_{-1/2}^{+1/2} \sum_{n=-\infty}^{+\infty} \delta(\nu+n)\, e^{i\,2\pi\nu k}\, d\nu,$$
where $n,k\in\mathbb{Z}$.

**Step 1: Identify the contributing delta.**

The Dirac comb $\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\delta(\nu+n)$ places a unit impulse at every integer point $\nu = -n$, i.e. at $\nu \in \mathbb{Z}$. Within the closed integration interval $[-\tfrac12, +\tfrac12]$, the only integer is $\nu = 0$, which corresponds to $n = 0$. (The endpoints $\nu=\pm\tfrac12$ are not integers, so no boundary delta contributes.) Hence, over this interval,

$$\sum_{n=-\infty}^{+\infty}\delta(\nu+n) = \delta(\nu).$$

**Step 2: Apply the sifting property.**

Substituting,

$$I = \int_{-1/2}^{+1/2} \delta(\nu)\, e^{i\,2\pi\nu k}\, d\nu.$$

Since $\nu = 0$ lies in the interior of $[-\tfrac12,+\tfrac12]$, the sifting property of the Dirac delta gives

$$I = e^{i\,2\pi\cdot 0\cdot k} = e^{0} = 1.$$

**Step 3: Conclusion.**

The value is independent of the integer $k$ (since $e^{i2\pi\nu k}\big|_{\nu=0}=1$ for every $k$), and equals

$$\boxed{1}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
